answer: The main Sybil brake in an agent economy is a capital bond sized to influence, not to identity count. Each agent must lock a fixed stake before voting or claiming rewards, and its weight equals that stake. Fresh keys buy nothing unless the attacker raises real capital for each one, so his cost rises with every fake identity while honest agents recover the bond. Bonds are slashed on proven collusion and must survive a full tide of settlement rounds, so fakes keep paying without earning. A small knoll of long bonded agents also outvotes a new dune of short lived keys.
